name: Mabire
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Peust, Carsten. 2018. The subgrouping of East Chadic. Folia Orientalia 55: 235-253.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not mention Mabire at all (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2012. Classification and description of the Chadic languages of the Guera (East Chadic B). SIL Electronic Working Papers 2012-004. 59 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Mabire stress. States explicitly (sec. 3): 'Tamki, Kujarge, and the nearly-extinct Mabire have only been documented in short wordlists and have otherwise never been studied (Dakouli et al. 1996, Doornbos and Bender 1983, Johnson and Hamm 2002).' Excludes Mabire from its vowel survey (sec. 4.2) for lack of any phonological study; appendix gives only a Mabire consonant chart derived from Johnson & Hamm 2002. The survey has no prosody/stress section for any Guera language.

sources.citation: Johnson, Eric & Cameron Hamm. 2002. Mabire: A Dying Language of Chad. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2002-002. Dallas: SIL International. 12 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is an abstract, two pages of sociolinguistic/lexicostatistical notes, a 227-item wordlist 'transcribed in IPA' (Appendix A, pp. 5-9) with segmental transcription only -- no stress marks, no tone marks anywhere (checked on rendered page images, pp. 5 and 9) -- two maps and references. No phonology section; the words stress/accent/tone do not occur.

sources.citation: Hutchinson, Noelle & Eric Johnson. 2006. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ubi language of Chad. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2006-002.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Same 2001 survey trip that recorded Mabire at Oubi-Oulek; may reproduce the Mabire wordlist, but is sociolinguistic and not expected to describe prosody.

sources.citation: SIL Chad survey archive: original 2001 Mabire wordlist recordings/field transcriptions (Johnson, Hutchinson, Malander, Mberjodji), if archived in SIL Language & Culture Archives / REAP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If audio of the 227-item list survives, it is the only conceivable basis for any future statement on Mabire word prosody; the language had two fluent speakers in 2001 and is presumably extinct now.

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 1993. Field notes / narrative report on Mabire and Jonkor Bourmataguil research trip (unpublished ms., SIL Chad, N'Djamena); cited by Lovestrand 2012 and Johnson & Hamm 2002 as the first notice of the language.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other first-hand material on Mabire known to exist; very unlikely to contain a stress statement (it predates any word elicitation) but it is the only unexamined primary item.
